scenario: LGRA.10.1.3's twin of LGRA.10.1.3_call_body_reads_after_withdraw: the same `call` and `on` body reading `{t.v}`, but the `call` comes before `withdraw t`. The capture is taken when the `call` runs ([LCCO.5.2]), while the fact is still there, so the body reads a value it captured legitimately. Compiles. It is also [LCYC.3.1.1]'s case of a `call` whose product the SCC does not consume: `withdraw t` makes `r` a one-rule SCC through its own withdraw edge ([LCYC.3.2.2]), and `r` carries a `call`, but no rule of the SCC matches the service's response schema `NotifySendReply` or `CallError`, so the SCC is admitted. PATH PINNED: the check's source order -- an action before the `withdraw` may refer to `t` freely, nested body included; and `dsc.cycle.lcyc_3_1_1_admitted`, where the call's outcomes (`emissions_of`) meet no match in the SCC.
rules_ds:
schema NotifySendReply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    status: Int

service notify.send:
    kwarg n: Int
    response NotifySendReply

schema Trig scope explicit:
    v: Int

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    call notify.send n: 1 cooldown: 30_s
        on response.status == 200:
            log info "sent {t.v}"
    withdraw t
